This is going to sound stupid at first, but...cashier. I used to have some terrible social anxiety, and being on register was torture for me. I would do absolutely anything to avoid it. I'd take out the trash or mop up baby barf to avoid it. Then one day I got sick of being anxious around people. The register became my place to grind for experience points. I've leveled-up so much that my new boss thinks I'm a "people person". He doesn't know how much it meant to me to hear that. I freaking love people!

I'm also terrible around people and most of my jobs have allowed me to isolate myself but I recently had an internship in which I had to work one on one with clients and that experience was amazing for me. I completely understand why your cashier job was so helpful for you.

Isn't it incredibly liberating? I'd obsessively try too hard to be liked, and I just came off as awkward and uncomfortable. Now I just go in assuming the person is cool, I listen to what they say, and the lack of obsessive perfection frees up the RAM and I can actually respond without trying.
